To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The microbiota of the upper respiratory tract is associated with asthma and allergic disease, and is altered in response to environmental factors, including exposure to tobacco smoke, antibiotics, and probiotics.
The environmental and airway microbiome in early childhood is associated with asthma risk and that these associations are mediated through the airway microbiome.

(1) the gut microbiome of healthy children is characterized by high diversity and low prevalence of pathogens; (2) the airway microbiome is characterized by high microbial diversity and a low abundance of potential pathogens; (3) the gut microbiota is associated with the airway microbiota; (4) the gut microbiomes of healthy children are characterized by a higher abundance of butyrate-producing bacteria and lower abundance of potentially proinflammatory bacteria, such as Enterobacteriaceae,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the environment and the microbiota on asthma and allergic disease.
the relationship between the microbiota of the airways and the environmental microbiota, and how this may be associated with asthma.
the role of the microbiota in asthma, particularly in early life.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microbiome is not the cause, nor the effect of asthma.
the role of the microbiota in asthma is complex, and that further studies are necessary before the microbiome can be used to predict, prevent or treat the disease.
there is an association between the microbiome and asthma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the environmental microbiome is associated with the mucosal microbiome in the upper airways and the gut, and that the gut microbiome in turn is associated with the upper airways, and this is associated with lower asthma prevalence.
the environmental microbial diversity is a key factor that influences asthma risk in childhood and that this operates through an altered mucosal microbiome.
we have found that the mucosal microbiota is not a mediator of the protective effect of farming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microbiome of the airways in early life is associated with the environment, and this association is mediated by a child's genetic predisposition.
the microbiome of the airways may be a key factor in the development and progression of asthma.
the environment is a major determinant of microbial diversity in the airways, and that this diversity is associated with lower asthma severity.
